relevance_note: The study includes 2 children with A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) with printed TNFAIP3 variants ('TNFAIP3: p. R271X', 'TNFAIP3: p. D70N'), described individually in Table 2 and Additional file 2.
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema (schema_ha20_v5.json) and extraction_rules_v1.md; nothing was taken from memory. The paper is a single-centre real-world study of 16 children with monogenic autoinflammatory diseases; only the 2 HA20 patients (and 2 HA20 patients quoted from the earlier report [17]) are in scope. Labels: patients are indexed by a bare-number column ('No'/'No.') in Table 2 and Additional file 2, but the text uses its own label for them ('3 patients (cases 4,12,13) were treated with thalidomide alone'), so rule 1 was applied and the labels are 'Case 12' and 'Case 13'; the alternative under the bare-number rule would be 'Table 2 #12'/'Table 2 #13'. No cell in any table uses ' / ' stacking, so no stacked-value situation arose. Table 1 reports per-disease-group counts only (HA20 column); the 0s there are counts in a table of counts and were not used to exclude anything, and the 1/2 counts (elevated CRP, elevated ESR, immunosuppressants, hydroxychloroquine) cannot be attributed to one of the two HA20 patients, so those items are 'not reported'. Additional file 2 gives 'Age at baseline in years' (11.50 and 5.75), which is the age at start of thalidomide, not onset, diagnosis or last evaluation, so no individual age was recorded in the individuals table. clinical_diagnosis_basis was taken from the study inclusion criterion 'a genetic diagnosis of monogenic AID' rather than from a per-patient statement. Mapping decisions: 'Fever' was mapped to the checklist item 'recurrent fever'; 'hypothyroidism' was mapped to 'autoimmune thyroiditis' although the paper does not call it autoimmune; 'punctate erosion of the rectum' was mapped to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'; 'multiple nodules in both lungs' was recorded as a phenotypic feature but NOT mapped to 'interstitial lung disease' (nodules are not interstitial disease). The group statement 'None of the patients had adverse events such as peripheral neuropathy and somnolence.' names the group and was used to mark peripheral neuropathy 'excluded' for the two in-study HA20 patients. The two HA20 patients of the earlier publication cited as [17] are mentioned in one Discussion sentence that gives features (gastrointestinal symptoms improved, glucocorticoids/biological agents, glucocorticoid withdrawal), so they were included under the v4 rule; no TNFAIP3 variant is printed for them, so no variants rows were created. No contradictions between statements about the same person were found.
